title: A Noetherian scheme has only finitely many points in a closed-point closed subset
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth] [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], and let $E\subseteq X$ be a closed subset. If every point of $E$ is closed in $X$, then $E$ is finite.

source.place: Properties Lemma 0BA8 (properties-lemma-Noetherian-irreducible-components), together with the definition of irreducibility and the fact that schemes are Kolmogorov

proof.text: By [lem-sc-noetherian-closed-subset-finite-components], the closed subset $E$ is the union of finitely many irreducible components $E_1,\ldots,E_r$, each irreducible and closed in $X$.

For each $i$, [lem-sc-scheme-sober] gives a generic point $\xi_i\in E_i$ with $E_i=\overline{\{\xi_i\}}$. By hypothesis $\xi_i$ is closed in $X$, so $\overline{\{\xi_i\}}=\{\xi_i\}$ and hence $E_i=\{\xi_i\}$.

Properties Lemma 0BA8, conclusion of the first paragraph
